n: Clark Clifford indicted for helping BCCI secretly take First American
rank: Chairman of First American Bankshares; former Secretary of Defense
d: Clark Clifford, Secretary of Defense under Lyndon Johnson, chaired First American, a Washington bank that the Bank of Credit and Commerce International (BCCI) secretly controlled. In July 1992 he and his law partner Robert Altman were indicted by federal and New York prosecutors on fraud and bribery charges for helping BCCI gain control of the bank while regulators were told BCCI was not involved. In late 1993 New York Justice John Bradley dismissed the state charges because Clifford's 'age and ill health' prevented a trial.
cite: Indictments by the Manhattan District Attorney and U.S. Justice Department, July 1992; New York Supreme Court dismissal, Nov 1993

arch.t: Bank of Credit and Commerce International — Abedi and Iqbal: BCCI Was the Largest Bank Fraud in History; CIA Used It for Covert Operations; 62 Countries Affected

n: BCCI's secret hold on First American; its president Altman acquitted
d: The Bank of Credit and Commerce International (BCCI) was charged with secretly taking over First American, a Washington bank, and prosecutors said Robert Altman, First American's president and the law partner of Clark Clifford, helped it do so and took bribes. The US Senate's BCCI report found that Clifford and Altman hid from regulators their own holdings of First American shares, which BCCI had financed. Altman was tried in New York on the charges, and a Manhattan jury acquitted him in August 1993.
cite: New York State Supreme Court jury verdict, August 1993; Senate 'BCCI Affair' report, 1992

arch.t: Bank of Credit and Commerce International — Abedi and Iqbal: BCCI Was the Largest Bank Fraud in History; CIA Used It for Covert Operations; 62 Countries Affected

n: BCCI paid debts of Carter's budget chief and paid Andrew Young
rank: Director of the Office of Management and Budget (Lance); UN Ambassador (Young)
d: The Bank of Credit and Commerce International (BCCI), a bank later closed worldwide for fraud, set out from 1977 to win friends in US politics, the US Senate's BCCI report found. It began by paying off the debts of Bert Lance, Jimmy Carter's former budget director, with a $3.5 million loan. It cultivated Carter, Jesse Jackson and Andrew Young, and the report described BCCI payments to Young while he was a public official as unusual and, by all appearances, improper. BCCI also hired former senators, congressmen, federal prosecutors and Federal Reserve lawyers, which helped slow investigations of the bank from 1988 to 1991.
cite: U.S. Senate Committee on Foreign Relations, 'The BCCI Affair', December 1992

arch.t: Bank of Credit and Commerce International — Abedi and Iqbal: BCCI Was the Largest Bank Fraud in History; CIA Used It for Covert Operations; 62 Countries Affected

n: BCCI took a California bank through Ghaith Pharaon with FDIC approval
d: The Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (FDIC), which insures deposits and approves some bank purchases, allowed Saudi businessman Ghaith Pharaon to buy Independence Bank in Encino, California, in 1985 while knowing of his ties to the Bank of Credit and Commerce International (BCCI) and that a senior BCCI officer would run the bank, the US Senate's BCCI report found. The FDIC did not consult the Federal Reserve or the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC). The report also found the OCC failed to pass on 1981 information that BCCI might be using nominees, or front owners, to buy US banks.
cite: U.S. Senate Committee on Foreign Relations, 'The BCCI Affair', December 1992

arch.t: Bank of Credit and Commerce International — Abedi and Iqbal: BCCI Was the Largest Bank Fraud in History; CIA Used It for Covert Operations; 62 Countries Affected

n: ALEC meeting drafted Arizona's SB 1070 immigration law
d: Corporate members of the American Legislative Exchange Council (ALEC) sat with Arizona legislators to draft the state's immigration law, SB 1070. ALEC is a US group where corporations pay to sit with state legislators and write 'model bills' that the legislators then introduce at home. NPR reported in October 2010 that SB 1070 was drafted at an ALEC meeting in December 2009 attended by legislators and corporate members, and that it became an ALEC model bill. Arizona enacted it in 2010, so a text written with corporate members in the room became state law. In 2012 the U.S. Supreme Court held parts of it preempted by federal law, meaning federal law overrode them.
cite: NPR investigation, October 2010; Arizona v. United States, 567 U.S. 387 (2012)

n: ALEC Exposed: 850 corporate-drafted model bills published
d: Corporations write bills for US state legislatures through the American Legislative Exchange Council (ALEC), where companies and state legislators draft 'model bills' together that legislators then file as their own. On 13 July 2011 the Center for Media and Democracy and The Nation published about 850 ALEC model bills from 30 years, with the legislators, corporations and states involved. About 1,000 ALEC-based bills were then being introduced each year, with roughly 20% enacted. ALEC's 'Stand Your Ground' model spread to about 30 states; after the 2012 killing of Trayvon Martin, more than 60 corporations and 34 legislators left ALEC. Common Cause filed an IRS complaint in April 2012 over its nonprofit status.
cite: Center for Media and Democracy, 'ALEC Exposed', 13 July 2011; Common Cause IRS complaint, April 2012

n: Gülen movement groups paid for about 200 congressional trips
rank: Members of Congress and their staff
d: Groups tied to the movement of Turkish cleric Fethullah Gülen paid for about 200 trips to Turkey for members of the US Congress and their staff since 2008, a USA Today investigation found. It identified 214 trips that appeared improperly disclosed, meaning Congress was not told who really paid. Some sponsors claimed nonprofit status that state and IRS records did not show, and five admitted a Gülen group in Turkey paid in-country costs. In July 2015 the House Ethics Committee, reviewing a related trip, found outside parties may have lied to it and referred the matter to the Justice Department.
cite: USA Today investigation, October 2015; House Committee on Ethics review, July 2015

n: Gülen-linked charter school staff gave clustered campaign donations
d: USA Today found clusters of campaign donations to members of the US Congress from Turkish Americans linked to the US charter schools of the movement of cleric Fethullah Gülen, which number over 100. Charter schools are publicly funded but privately run. The pattern suggested money was being channelled through individuals. Sen. Kelly Ayotte refunded $43,100 given on a single day by 19 out-of-state donors, five of whom could not be located. Rep. Henry Cuellar received nine $2,500 donations on one day, including one from a Toledo charter school teacher earning about $37,000 a year.
cite: USA Today investigation, November 2015 (via Religion News Service)

n: Hochul aide Linda Sun charged with secretly working for China
rank: Deputy chief of staff to the Governor of New York
d: Linda Sun, deputy chief of staff to New York Governor Kathy Hochul (2021–22) after serving in Andrew Cuomo's administration, was charged on 3 September 2024 with acting as an illegal agent of China, along with visa fraud and money laundering; her husband Chris Hu was also charged. Prosecutors allege she blocked contact between the governor's office and Taiwan's representatives, steered messaging on Uyghurs, and worked with the Henan Association of Eastern America, a group affiliated with China's united front influence system, to arrange a Hochul visit to Henan. The trial ended in a mistrial on 22 December 2025 after the jury deadlocked; prosecutors said they would retry.
cite: United States v. Linda Sun and Chris Hu, U.S. District Court, Eastern District of New York (indicted 2024; mistrial Dec 2025)

n: Arcadia mayor Eileen Wang pleads guilty as a Chinese agent
rank: Mayor and city council member, Arcadia, California
d: Eileen Wang, who was elected to the Arcadia City Council in California in November 2022 and later became mayor, pleaded guilty to acting as an illegal agent of the People's Republic of China. From 2020 to 2022, with her then-fiancé Yaoning 'Mike' Sun, she ran the website U.S. News Center and posted pro-Beijing material on the orders of PRC officials, including an essay denying abuses in Xinjiang. Sun ran her council campaign at the Chinese government's direction. She was charged on 11 May 2026 and resigned. Prosecutors said her work for Beijing stopped after she was sworn in.
cite: U.S. Attorney's Office, Central District of California, charge 11 May 2026; guilty plea May 2026
org_note: prc_state = PRC government officials or intelligence acting through local proxies, where the forum did not name the United Front Work Department

n: Mike Sun ran an Arcadia council campaign on Beijing's orders
d: Yaoning 'Mike' Sun organised a team to help elect Eileen Wang to the Arcadia City Council in California in November 2022, acting as her campaign treasurer, at the direction of the Chinese government. He pleaded guilty in October 2025 to acting as an illegal agent of a foreign government and is serving four years in federal prison. The Justice Department said Wang had dealt with John Chen, described as a high-level member of the PRC intelligence apparatus, who was sentenced in 2024 to 20 months.
cite: U.S. District Court, Central District of California, guilty plea Oct 2025
org_note: prc_state = PRC government officials or intelligence acting through local proxies, where the forum did not name the United Front Work Department

n: Suspected Chinese operative Fang Fang placed an intern with Swalwell
rank: Office of a U.S. Representative on the House Intelligence Committee
d: Fang Fang (Christine Fang), believed by US officials to be a Chinese intelligence operative, built ties with California politicians from 2011 to 2015, Axios reported in December 2020. She raised money for the campaign of Rep. Eric Swalwell, later a member of the House Intelligence Committee, and placed at least one intern in his office, while keeping close contact with the Chinese consulate in San Francisco. She left the US abruptly in 2015. No charges were filed, and the reporting did not accuse Swalwell of wrongdoing.
cite: Axios investigation, December 2020; follow-up reporting
org_note: prc_state = PRC government officials or intelligence acting through local proxies, where the forum did not name the United Front Work Department

n: Han Dong's 2019 nomination and suspected Chinese consulate role
d: China's consulate in Toronto was suspected of helping steer the 2019 Liberal nomination of Han Dong in the Toronto riding of Don Valley North. Canada's Special Rapporteur David Johnston found 'irregularities' in the nomination and a 'well-grounded suspicion' that they were tied to the consulate of the People's Republic of China, but no evidence Dong knew. Intelligence said international students were bused to the vote; Dong said a school arranged the bus. Dong left the Liberal caucus in March 2023. Johnston found false the claim that Dong urged China to delay freeing Michael Kovrig and Michael Spavor; the Hogue Commission report corroborated Dong's denial, and in August 2025 the Commissioner of Canada Elections found no breach of election law in the nomination.
cite: Independent Special Rapporteur on Foreign Interference (Johnston), first report, May 2023; Public Inquiry into Foreign Interference (Hogue Commission), 2024–25; Commissioner of Canada Elections, Aug 2025
org_note: prc_state = PRC government officials or intelligence acting through local proxies, where the forum did not name the United Front Work Department

n: Foreign states drew 'witting' Canadian MPs into interference
d: Foreign states, chiefly China and Russia, with India, Pakistan and Iran also active, drew some Canadian MPs and senators into their interference, according to Canada's National Security and Intelligence Committee of Parliamentarians (NSICOP), a committee of MPs and senators cleared to read secret intelligence. Its June 2024 report said some unnamed parliamentarians were 'semi-witting or witting participants'. The conduct listed included accepting disguised funds from foreign missions or their proxies, passing colleagues' views to foreign diplomats, and giving confidential government information to a known foreign intelligence officer. The Hogue Commission's final report in January 2025 found no evidence of 'traitors' in Parliament plotting with foreign states.
cite: National Security and Intelligence Committee of Parliamentarians, special report on foreign interference, 3 June 2024; Hogue Commission final report, 28 Jan 2025
org_note: foreign_state = state-directed influence networks of several countries (China, India and others) as described by NSICOP, not a single named organisation

n: Klan member Hugo Black reached the Supreme Court undisclosed
rank: Associate Justice of the U.S. Supreme Court
d: The Ku Klux Klan, a white-supremacist secret order, had a life member reach the US Supreme Court without the public knowing. Hugo Black joined the Klan in September 1923, resigned in July 1925 as he began his Senate run, and was welcomed back with a life membership in September 1926 during the campaign. The membership was not public when he was confirmed to the Court in 1937. Weeks later Ray Sprigle of the Pittsburgh Post-Gazette exposed it and won a Pulitzer Prize. In a radio address on 1 October 1937 Black said: 'I did join the Klan. I later resigned. I never rejoined.' He served on the Court until 1971.
cite: Pittsburgh Post-Gazette (Ray Sprigle), Sept 1937; Black's radio address, 1 Oct 1937
org_note: kkk = Ku Klux Klan (secret fraternal order with state-office reach in the 1920s)

arch.t: US Supreme Court Justice Was Documented KKK Member; Alabama KKK-Masonic Network Used as Political Infrastructure to Reach Highest Judicial Office

n: Klan chapter leader Robert Byrd entered office and the Senate
rank: U.S. Senator (West Virginia); West Virginia House of Delegates
d: Robert Byrd organised and led a 150-member Ku Klux Klan chapter in West Virginia in the early 1940s as its 'Exalted Cyclops', the chapter head, and was a recruiter ('Kleagle') until early 1943. A 1946 letter shows his continued involvement in the year he was elected to the West Virginia House of Delegates. He went on to the U.S. House in 1952 and the Senate in 1958, and when he died in 2010 he had served in the Senate longer than anyone. He called the membership a 'sad mistake'.
cite: Byrd's own statements and 2005 memoir; PolitiFact review of the record, 2019
org_note: kkk = Ku Klux Klan (secret fraternal order with state-office reach in the 1920s)

n: Indiana Klan's governor tried for bribe offer to place Klansmen
d: D. C. Stephenson, Grand Dragon (state leader) of the Indiana Ku Klux Klan, which had about 250,000 members, backed Ed Jackson, who won the governorship in 1924. After Stephenson was sentenced to life in 1925 for the death of Madge Oberholtzer, he gave evidence to the Indianapolis Times. Jackson was tried in 1928 for offering Governor Warren McCray a $10,000 bribe in 1923 on Stephenson's behalf to fill state offices with Klansmen. The trial ended with a hung jury, and the statute of limitations barred a conviction. Stephenson's evidence also ended the career of Indianapolis Mayor John Duvall.
cite: Marion County criminal proceedings, 1927–28; Indianapolis Times investigation (Pulitzer Prize, 1928)
org_note: kkk = Ku Klux Klan (secret fraternal order with state-office reach in the 1920s)

n: Klansman mayor of Denver made a Klansman police chief
rank: Mayor of Denver; Denver police chief
d: Benjamin Stapleton was Ku Klux Klan member number 1,128 when he ran for mayor of Denver in 1923, historian Robert Alan Goldberg found. Under Klan pressure he appointed Klansman William Candlish police chief, and the police department became in effect a Klan body. In the 1924 recall election the Klan gave his campaign more than $15,000, and he told a Klan rally he would work 'heart and soul' for it. In 1925 Stapleton broke with the Klan and fired Candlish.
cite: Robert Alan Goldberg, Hooded Empire: The Ku Klux Klan in Colorado (1981)
org_note: kkk = Ku Klux Klan (secret fraternal order with state-office reach in the 1920s)

n: Colorado Klan won the governorship and state House in 1924
rank: Governor of Colorado; U.S. Senator; state House majority
d: The Ku Klux Klan, a white-supremacist secret society, got its members into Colorado's governorship and a majority of the state House in the 1924 election. The new governor, Clarence Morley, was a Klan member who took direction from the Klan's Grand Dragon (state leader), John Galen Locke. Rice Means won a US Senate seat with open Klan support. Klan-backed bills proposed firing Catholic and Jewish faculty at the University of Colorado, but a state Senate group led by Billy Adams blocked most of them. Morley and Locke both later went to jail.
cite: Robert Alan Goldberg, Hooded Empire (1981); Colorado Independent historical reporting
org_note: kkk = Ku Klux Klan (secret fraternal order with state-office reach in the 1920s)

n: Oregon Klan backed Governor Pierce in return for its school law
d: In 1922 the Ku Klux Klan in Oregon backed Democrat Walter M. Pierce for governor after its own candidate lost the Republican primary. In return Pierce agreed to support the Klan's Compulsory Education Act, and he won with 57% of the vote. The act, passed by voters the same year, would have forced children into public schools and was aimed at Catholic schools. The U.S. Supreme Court struck it down in Pierce v. Society of Sisters (1925).
cite: Oregon election records, 1922; Pierce v. Society of Sisters, 268 U.S. 510 (1925)
org_note: kkk = Ku Klux Klan (secret fraternal order with state-office reach in the 1920s)

n: Klan members inside Fruitland Park, Florida police
rank: Deputy police chief and police officer
d: Deputy Chief David Borst and Officer George Hunnewell of the police department in Fruitland Park, Florida, had been involved with the Ku Klux Klan between 2005 and 2009, an unrelated FBI investigation found; three informants linked Hunnewell. The FBI told the Florida Department of Law Enforcement, which informed the police chief in 2014. Borst resigned and Hunnewell was fired. The Lake County State Attorney's office, which prosecutes cases in the county, began reviewing their arrests for racial profiling, meaning targeting people because of their race.
cite: Florida Department of Law Enforcement report based on FBI information, July 2014
org_note: kkk = Ku Klux Klan (secret fraternal order with state-office reach in the 1920s)

n: FBI warned white supremacists were placing 'ghost skins' in police
d: An October 2006 FBI intelligence assessment warned that white supremacist groups had a 'historical' interest in infiltrating or recruiting police, and that this 'can lead to investigative breaches', such as leaks about inquiries. It described 'ghost skins', members who hide their beliefs to blend in, and at least one skinhead group urging them to seek police jobs. An April 2015 FBI counterterrorism policy guide said investigations of militia, white supremacist and sovereign citizen extremists had often found active links to law enforcement officers.
cite: FBI Intelligence Assessment, 'White Supremacist Infiltration of Law Enforcement', 17 Oct 2006; FBI Counterterrorism Policy Guide, April 2015 (published by The Intercept, 2017)
org_note: white_supremacist = organised white supremacist groups (Klan, skinhead and similar), as named by the FBI

n: Masonic sheriff convicted in abduction of ex-Mason William Morgan
rank: Sheriff of Niagara County, New York
d: Freemasons used their members in local office to silence William Morgan of Batavia, New York, who had announced a book exposing Masonic rituals. He was jailed in Canandaigua on minor charges on 11 September 1826, taken away by men on the night of 12 September, brought to Fort Niagara, and never seen again. Niagara County Sheriff Eli Bruce, a Mason, was removed from office and convicted of conspiracy for his part, serving 28 months; Loton Lawson, Nicholas Chesebro and Edward Sawyer were also convicted. Public anger at the light sentences led to the Anti-Masonic Party, which ran a presidential candidate in 1832.
cite: New York state criminal trials, 1827–1831 (People v. Bruce and related cases)
org_note: freemasonry here = Batavia and western New York lodges

arch.t: Anti-Masonic Party — First Third Party in US History; Formed After Murder of Military Witness; New York State Investigation Confirmed Masonic Obstruction of Justice

n: Secret Know Nothing order took the Massachusetts government
rank: Governor and the entire state legislature of Massachusetts
d: The Order of the Star Spangled Banner, a secret anti-immigrant fraternal order whose members were told to answer 'I know nothing' when asked about it, took over the government of Massachusetts through the political movement it gave rise to, the Know Nothings. In the 1854 election the Know Nothings won the governorship (Henry Gardner), all 40 state Senate seats and all but 3 of the House seats. The 1855 legislature then passed laws to deport poor or mentally ill Irish residents and to 'inspect' Catholic schools and convents, and required Protestant Bible readings in public schools. The results are recorded in the state's election returns and legislative records.
cite: Massachusetts election returns, 1854; Massachusetts legislative records, 1855
org_note: know_nothing = the Order of the Star Spangled Banner, a secret nativist fraternal order and its American Party

n: Tammany Society's 'Boss' Tweed ran and robbed New York City
rank: New York state senator and city Commissioner of Public Works
d: The Tammany Society, a New York political club, gave William M. Tweed control of New York City government after he became its Grand Sachem, or head, in 1863. Through Tammany he ran the city while holding seats in Congress, the county Board of Supervisors and the state Senate, and serving as Commissioner of Public Works. At his retrial in November 1873 he was convicted on 204 of 220 counts and sentenced to 12 years and a $12,750 fine; a higher court cut the sentence to one year. A New York aldermen's committee in 1877 estimated he had stolen $25–45 million from the city.
cite: New York Court of Oyer and Terminer, People v. Tweed, Nov 1873; New York Board of Aldermen report, 1877
org_note: tammany = the Society of St. Tammany, a fraternal society with ritual offices (sachems) that ran the New York Democratic machine

n: Orange Order members held Toronto city hall for over a century
rank: Mayor of Toronto and city council
d: The Loyal Orange Institution, or Orange Order, is a Protestant fraternal order that worked to keep its members in public office. By 1844 six of Toronto's ten aldermen (city councillors) were Orangemen, and 20 of its 23 mayors in the 19th century were members. Every Toronto mayor in the first half of the 20th century was an Orangeman, and in 1942 16 of 23 council members were. The run ended in 1954, when Nathan Phillips beat Orange leader Leslie Saunders; William Dennison (1967–72) was the last Orange mayor.
cite: William J. Smyth, Toronto, the Belfast of Canada: The Orange Order and the Shaping of Municipal Culture (University of Toronto Press, 2015)
org_note: orange_order = Loyal Orange Institution (Protestant fraternal lodge)

n: Orange Order: four Canadian prime ministers, one a Grand Master
d: The Orange Order, a Protestant fraternal order that worked to place its members in public office in Canada, counted four Canadian prime ministers among its members: Sir John A. Macdonald, Sir John Abbott, Sir Mackenzie Bowell and John Diefenbaker. Bowell, prime minister in 1894–96, was a past Grand Master, or overall head, of the Orange Order in British North America, so the order's former leader ran the federal government. The memberships are recorded in the order's Canadian records as summarised in academic and reference histories.
cite: Orange Order in Canada membership records as summarised in academic and reference histories
org_note: orange_order = Loyal Orange Institution (Protestant fraternal lodge)

n: Secret Ordre de Jacques-Cartier placed francophones in federal posts
rank: Senior federal public service posts; Montreal mayor's office
d: The Ordre de Jacques-Cartier, called 'La Patente', was a secret society founded on 22 October 1926 in Vanier (now part of Ottawa) to advance French Canadians and counter the Orange Order, Freemasons and Knights of Columbus. It recruited decision-makers, including Montreal mayor Jean Drapeau and journalist-politician Pierre Laporte, and used the network to get francophones appointed to key federal public service jobs. It peaked at 11,300 members in 1955–56. After a former insider, Roger Cyr, exposed it in a 1964 book, it dissolved in February 1965.
cite: The Canadian Encyclopedia, 'Ordre de Jacques Cartier'; Roger Cyr, La Patente (1964)
org_note: jacques_cartier = Ordre de Jacques-Cartier, a secret French-Canadian Catholic society (1926–65)

n: Commons committee urged Freemasons in police and courts to register
rank: judges, magistrates, police officers, Crown prosecutors
d: Freemasons hold posts across the police and courts of England and Wales, and in March 1997 the House of Commons Home Affairs Committee published 'Freemasonry in the Police and the Judiciary'. Freemasonry is a fraternal society whose members meet in private lodges. The report counted nearly 350,000 masons in 7,835 lodges in England and Wales under the United Grand Lodge of England. It recommended that police officers, judges, magistrates and Crown prosecutors register membership of the Freemasons or any other secret society, stating that 'nothing so much undermines public confidence in public institutions' as public servants belonging to one. The Association of Chief Police Officers refused to back a register; Lord Chancellor Lord Mackay opposed compulsory disclosure for judges.
cite: House of Commons Home Affairs Committee, 'Freemasonry in the Police and the Judiciary', Third Report 1996–97 (March 1997)

arch.t: UK Investigation: Masonic Network in Police and Judiciary Led to Parliamentary Inquiry and New Legal Disclosure Requirements

n: Freemasons among judges; Grand Lodge stalled on police squad list
rank: detectives of the West Midlands Serious Crime Squad
d: Freemasons made up an estimated 5–10% of professional judges and 5–20% of magistrates in England and Wales, the House of Commons Home Affairs Committee said in its second report on Freemasonry (May 1999). Freemasonry is a fraternal society whose members meet privately in lodges and swear oaths of mutual support. The Committee said it obtained the cooperation of the United Grand Lodge of England, the masons' governing body, only 'through compulsion' after 'months of prevarication and obfuscation'. The Grand Lodge needed five attempts to produce a list of masons in the West Midlands Serious Crime Squad, a police unit disbanded in 1989, and the Committee doubted the final list was complete. It called the government's voluntary police register inadequate.
cite: House of Commons Home Affairs Committee, Freemasonry in Public Life, Second Report 1998–99 (May 1999), as reported by SQUALL magazine

arch.t: UK Investigation: Masonic Network in Police and Judiciary Led to Parliamentary Inquiry and New Legal Disclosure Requirements

n: 205 judges and 1,900 magistrates were masons when declaration ended
d: Freemasons, members of a fraternal society organised in lodges whose members pledge mutual help, held 205 of the 3,808 judges' posts in England and Wales (5.4%) and 1,900 of the 29,702 magistrates' posts (6.4%), Ministry of Justice figures showed in 2009. Since 1998 applicants for judicial office had had to declare Masonic membership. The United Grand Lodge of England made representations against the rule in May 2009, citing the European Court of Human Rights cases Grande Oriente d'Italia di Palazzo Giustiniani v Italy (no. 1 and no. 2), and on 5 November 2009 Justice Secretary Jack Straw ended it. The review found no evidence of impropriety arising from judges being masons.
cite: Written ministerial statement, Secretary of State for Justice, 5 November 2009

n: 397 Met Police officers and staff declare they are Freemasons
d: Freemasons hold posts inside London's Metropolitan Police: 397 officers and staff declared membership of the Freemasons or similar hierarchical organisations by February 2026, once the force required it. The Met decided on 18 November 2025, and announced on 11 December 2025, that such membership would be a declarable association for its officers and staff; most of those who declared were Freemasons. The United Grand Lodge of England, the governing body of English Freemasonry, sought judicial review, a court challenge to the decision. On 17 February 2026 Mr Justice Chamberlain refused permission on all grounds, finding the requirement a proportionate way to maintain public trust in policing.
cite: R (United Grand Lodge of England) v Commissioner of Police of the Metropolis [2026] EWHC 330 (Admin); Judiciary press summary, 17 February 2026

arch.t: UK Investigation: Masonic Network in Police and Judiciary Led to Parliamentary Inquiry and New Legal Disclosure Requirements

n: MI5 says Christine Lee covertly worked for China through MPs
rank: Members of Parliament (Barry Gardiner MP's office)
d: The Chinese Communist Party reached into Britain's Parliament through London solicitor Christine Lee, according to MI5, Britain's domestic security service. On 13 January 2022 MI5 issued an interference alert, circulated by the Speaker to MPs, stating that Lee had acted covertly in coordination with the party's United Front Work Department, the body that builds its influence abroad. Labour MP Barry Gardiner had received donations from her, the last in June 2020, and her son worked in his office as diary manager until he resigned that week. Lee challenged the alert; on 17 December 2024 the Investigatory Powers Tribunal ruled that MI5 had issued it for legitimate reasons.
cite: MI5 Interference Alert, 13 January 2022; Investigatory Powers Tribunal judgment, 17 December 2024

n: China's Communist Party reached the royal circle through Yang Tengbo
rank: Duke of York (member of the royal family)
d: The Chinese Communist Party reached into the British royal circle through businessman Yang Tengbo, the UK Home Office concluded. The Home Office believed he may have worked for the United Front Work Department, the party body that builds influence abroad. Through Prince Andrew he had been a guest at royal residences, and he had met former prime ministers David Cameron and Theresa May. In March 2023 Home Secretary Suella Braverman barred him from the UK for 'covert and deceptive activity' on behalf of the party. In December 2024 the Special Immigration Appeals Commission upheld the exclusion; its judges said there was 'not an abundance of evidence' of United Front links but found he had played down his ties to the party.
cite: Home Office exclusion order, March 2023; Special Immigration Appeals Commission judgment, December 2024

n: Le Cercle chaired by MPs sitting on the Foreign Affairs Committee
rank: members of the Commons Foreign Affairs Committee
d: Two MPs sitting on the House of Commons Foreign Affairs Select Committee, which scrutinises UK foreign policy, chaired Le Cercle, a private foreign-policy club, without declaring the role to Parliament, PoliticsHome reported in 2019. They were Rory Stewart (chair 2013–14) and Nadhim Zahawi (2015–18). Le Cercle, founded in 1952–53, brings politicians, intelligence figures and business people together in private. Its earlier UK chairs were also sitting politicians: Julian Amery (1985–93), Jonathan Aitken (1993–96), Norman Lamont (1996–2008) and Michael Ancram (2008–13). Because the chairmanships were not declared, MPs examining government foreign policy held a leading role in a private network that Parliament and the public did not know about.
cite: PoliticsHome (John Johnston), 2019; David Teacher, Rogue Agents: The Cercle and the 6I in the Private Cold War (2003)

n: Knights of St Columbanus members in Costello's Irish cabinet
org_note: Knights of Saint Columbanus: Catholic fraternal order founded in Ireland in 1915, long described as secretive.
d: Members of the Knights of Saint Columbanus, a Catholic fraternal order founded in Ireland in 1915 and long described as secretive, sat in Ireland's government from 1948. John A. Costello, Taoiseach (prime minister) of the first Inter-Party government from 1948, was a Knight, as were other members of his cabinet; that government gave Maynooth seminary a special annual grant. Labour parliamentary chairman William Davin TD, also a Knight, is reported to have countered support within government for the Mother and Child health scheme, a plan for free state care of mothers and children that Archbishop John Charles McQuaid opposed. These accounts rest chiefly on John Cooney's biography of McQuaid (1999) and Anthony Jordan's biography of Costello (2007).
cite: John Cooney, John Charles McQuaid: Ruler of Catholic Ireland (1999); Anthony Jordan, John A. Costello 1891–1976 (2007)

n: Justice Minister Seán MacEoin gave assurances to the Knights' council
org_note: Knights of Saint Columbanus: Catholic fraternal order founded in Ireland in 1915.
d: The Knights of Saint Columbanus, a Catholic fraternal order founded in Ireland in 1915, had a member in charge of Ireland's justice ministry. Seán MacEoin, Minister for Justice in 1948, belonged to the Order and reportedly assured its governing Supreme Council that efforts would be made to prevent conflict between Church and State, giving a private religious body undertakings on government conduct. The Order also had members in the civil service, including Dublin City chief planner Michael O'Brien and the Taxing Master of the Courts, Henry B. O'Hanlon, the official who assesses legal costs. The account comes from John Cooney's 1999 biography of Archbishop John Charles McQuaid.
cite: John Cooney, John Charles McQuaid: Ruler of Catholic Ireland (1999)

n: Grand Orient lodges filed on French officers to steer promotions
rank: Minister of War (General Louis André) and army promotions
d: Members of the Grand Orient de France, the country's largest Masonic body, reported on army officers to the War Ministry, which used the reports to decide promotions. Between 1901 and 1904 the ministry of General Louis André filed Catholic and nationalist officers as 'Carthage', generally blocking them, and republican officers as 'Corinth', favouring them. Grand Orient secretary-general Narcisse-Amédée Vadecard received the reports and Captain Henri Mollin ran the system in André's office. Historian Serge Berstein counted 18,818 files written between September 1901 and October 1903, out of about 27,000 active officers. Deputy Jean Guyot de Villeneuve exposed the scheme in the Chamber on 28 October 1904; André resigned on 15 November 1904 and the Combes government fell on 15 January 1905.
cite: Chamber of Deputies session, 28 October 1904; Serge Berstein (historian), cited in standard histories of the Third Republic

n: Manuel Valls, later Prime Minister, was a Grand Orient lodge member
rank: mayor of Évry and National Assembly deputy (later Interior Minister and Prime Minister)
d: Manuel Valls belonged to the Grand Orient de France, the country's largest Masonic body, while he rose into elected office. According to L'Express, he was initiated into the Grand Orient lodge 'Ni maîtres ni dieux' on 26 April 1989, moved in 1995 to 'L'Infini maçonnique', a lodge founded by Alain Bauer, and his resignation was recorded in 2005. During that period he became mayor of Évry (2001) and a National Assembly deputy (2002). After leaving he served as Interior Minister (2012) and Prime Minister (2014). Valls declined to answer L'Express's questions.
cite: L'Express, reproduced by Seneweb

n: Secret NATO money funded Belgium's stay-behind network
rank: military intelligence (SDRA VIII) and State Security (STC/Mob)
d: NATO secretly paid for Belgium's 'stay-behind' network, which sat inside the country's military intelligence and State Security services. Stay-behind networks were secret organisations set up in NATO countries after the Second World War to resist a possible Soviet occupation. Belgium's was coordinated by a secretariat (SDRA XI) funded by secret NATO payments, with a military section (SDRA VIII) under military intelligence and the Defence Minister, and a civilian section (STC/Mob) under State Security and the Justice Minister. It was made public on 7 November 1990 and the government decided to disband it on 23 November 1990. A Senate commission chaired by Roger Lallemand heard 37 witnesses in 1991. It criticised the refusal to name civilian operatives; former SDRA head Paul Detrembleur refused to testify about the secretariat.
cite: Belgian Senate Commission of Inquiry into the stay-behind network (Lallemand commission), report 1991

arch.t: Italy — Operation Gladio: NATO Stay-Behind Network Used for Domestic Terrorism; 'Strategy of Tension'

n: Neo-Nazi Westland New Post had members in gendarmerie and at NATO
org_note: Westland New Post: Belgian far-right paramilitary group founded by Paul Latinus with Front de la Jeunesse members.
rank: Gendarmerie (Diane anti-terror unit) and State Security
d: Westland New Post (WNP), a Belgian neo-Nazi group of the early 1980s, had members inside the Gendarmerie, Belgium's national police, and at a NATO site. Former gendarme Martin Leukeu said he was recruited into 'Group G', a neo-Nazi cell inside the Gendarmerie linked to WNP, and gendarme Madani Bouhouche was named as a member. NATO documents from the Evere transmission centre, passed by member Michel Libert, were found at member Marcel Barbier's home. Belgium's State Security service was also entangled: WNP founder Paul Latinus had been its informant, State Security agent Christian Smets admitted training members in surveillance, and the service had a mole in the group from 1981 but did not tell police. A parliamentary inquiry found no proof of a conspiracy behind the Brabant killings, a series of 1980s armed raids.
cite: Belgian parliamentary inquiries into the Nijvel (Brabant) gang and banditry; David Teacher, Rogue Agents (2003)

n: British intelligence worked closely with Swiss secret army P-26
d: British intelligence services worked closely with P-26, a secret Swiss resistance organisation inside the Swiss defence department that operated outside parliamentary and government control until 1990, although Switzerland is officially neutral and outside NATO. Judge Pierre Cornu's official report, of roughly 100 pages, found this extensive cooperation and also found that P-26 lacked political or legal legitimacy. Only a 17-page summary, titled 'P-26 not part of an international network', was published on 19 September 1991. Defence Minister Kaspar Villiger refused to release the full report, which remains sealed until 2041 despite parliamentary motions in 2005 and 2008, so the extent of British involvement is still not public.
cite: Report of Judge Pierre Cornu to the Federal Council, 1991 (summary published 19 September 1991)

n: Reichsbürger coup plot had a sitting judge and ex-MP inside
org_note: Patriotic Union / 'Council' around Heinrich XIII Prinz Reuss: Reichsbürger network charged by the Federal Prosecutor as a terrorist association.
rank: judge at the Berlin Regional Court; former Bundestag member
d: A group of 'Reichsbürger', people who reject the legitimacy of the modern German state, around Heinrich XIII Prinz Reuss had a serving judge among its leaders. Birgit Malsack-Winkemann, a judge at the Berlin Regional Court and AfD Bundestag member for about four years, was arrested in the December 2022 raids. Prosecutors say she was to be justice minister in a new government; she admits being on the group's 'Council' with responsibility for justice. As a former MP she could bring up to six people into the Reichstag, and admits leading co-accused through it twice in September 2022. Prosecutors say up to 16 people, mainly from the KSK and other special units, were to storm it. Twenty-six defendants have been on trial since 2024; no verdict had been reported as of April 2026.
cite: Federal Prosecutor General indictment; Federal Court of Justice detention ruling (2023); Higher Regional Court Frankfurt trial from May 2024

n: Russian-funded Voice of Europe: AfD MP Bystron investigated
org_note: Voice of Europe: Prague-based pro-Russian outlet and influence network financed by Viktor Medvedchuk, sanctioned by the Czech government in March 2024.
rank: Bundestag member, then Member of the European Parliament
d: Voice of Europe, a news website operating from Prague that Czech intelligence says was financed from Russia, is suspected of paying European politicians, including German MP Petr Bystron of the AfD party. Czech intelligence (BIS) briefed the Czech parliament's intelligence committee on a recording of a Prague meeting with Artem Marchevsky, whom the Czech government sanctioned as part of the network, in which about €20,000 was reportedly handed over. In April 2024 the Munich prosecutor's office opened a bribery and money-laundering investigation into Bystron. The Bundestag lifted his immunity and police searched his parliamentary office in May 2024. After he became a member of the European Parliament, it lifted his immunity on 6 May 2025. Bystron denies receiving money; no charge had been reported.
cite: Munich I Public Prosecutor's investigation; Bundestag immunity decision (May 2024); European Parliament immunity vote, 6 May 2025

n: Czech government exposes Russian-funded Voice of Europe payments
org_note: Voice of Europe: Prague-based pro-Russian outlet and influence network financed by Viktor Medvedchuk.
d: Voice of Europe, a news website operating from the Czech Republic, was used to pass Russian money to European politicians, according to Czech intelligence and press reports. The BIS security service said the network was financed from Russia and operated on Czech territory. On 27 March 2024 Petr Fiala's government put Voice of Europe, Viktor Medvedchuk, a pro-Russian Ukrainian politician, and Artyom Marchevsky on the Czech national sanctions list, which freezes assets and bans dealings with them. Deník N, citing a foreign ministry source, reported that payments went to politicians from Belgium, France, Germany, Hungary, the Netherlands and Poland, in particular the AfD. The case led Munich prosecutors to investigate AfD MP Petr Bystron for bribery; he denies receiving money.
cite: Czech government sanctions decision, 27 March 2024; Security Information Service (BIS) statement

n: Thule Society members Hess and Frank rose into the Nazi government
rank: Deputy Führer (Hess); Reich minister and later Governor-General of occupied Poland (Frank)
d: The Thule Society, a German nationalist and occultist lodge formed in Munich in 1918 around Rudolf von Sebottendorff's lodge, had members who later held top posts in Nazi Germany. Historian Nicholas Goodrick-Clarke states that Rudolf Hess and Hans Frank were members before they rose in the Nazi Party, while Alfred Rosenberg, Dietrich Eckart and Gottfried Feder attended only as guests. He calls longer membership lists that include Hitler and others 'spurious'. Hess became Deputy Führer, Hitler's deputy as party leader, in 1933; Frank became a Reich minister and, from 1939, Governor-General of occupied Poland.
cite: Nicholas Goodrick-Clarke, The Occult Roots of Nazism (1985, later editions)

n: Sweden's secret IB spy bureau reported to the ruling party
org_note: Informationsbyrån (IB): Swedish military intelligence unit with no official status, which registered and infiltrated the far left; directed by Birger Elmér.
rank: military intelligence; Prime Minister and Social Democratic party secretary
d: IB, a secret Swedish military intelligence bureau with no official status, was reported to answer to leaders of the governing Social Democratic Party as well as to the military. On 3 May 1973 journalists Jan Guillou and Peter Bratt revealed in Folket i Bild/Kulturfront that IB monitored and registered people with far-left views and infiltrated left-wing groups, including break-ins at the Communist Party's offices. Former security chief P.G. Vinge wrote that IB director Birger Elmér had regular contact with Prime Minister Olof Palme and reported to Social Democratic party secretary Sven Andersson; Palme denied any link. The journalists, not IB staff, were convicted of espionage on 4 January 1974. A 2002 public inquiry report, 'Rikets säkerhet och den personliga integriteten', set out IB's operations.
cite: Swedish court verdict, 4 January 1974; Swedish government inquiry report 'Rikets säkerhet och den personliga integriteten' (2002)

n: Ordo Iuris founder made Polish deputy foreign minister
org_note: Ordo Iuris Institute for Legal Culture: Polish Catholic-conservative legal think tank founded in 2013 by the Christian Culture Association.
d: Ordo Iuris, a Polish conservative Catholic legal think tank that drafts laws and campaigns to change policy, had its founder placed in government. Aleksander Stępkowski co-founded Ordo Iuris in 2013 and chaired its management board from 2013 to 2015. In November 2015 the new Law and Justice government of Beata Szydło appointed him deputy foreign minister for legal and treaty affairs, responsible for international agreements; he left the Ordo Iuris chair in December 2015. He was recalled in August 2016. In 2016 Ordo Iuris drafted a near-total abortion ban that the Sejm rejected on 6 October 2016 after nationwide protests.
cite: Polish government appointment records; Forsal; Ruleoflaw.pl

n: Ordo Iuris co-founder made acting head of Polish Supreme Court
org_note: Ordo Iuris Institute for Legal Culture: Polish Catholic-conservative legal think tank founded in 2013.
rank: acting First President of the Supreme Court
d: Ordo Iuris, a Polish conservative Catholic legal think tank that campaigns to change law and policy, had its co-founder placed at the head of the country's highest court. Aleksander Stępkowski, Ordo Iuris co-founder and board president in 2013–2015 and 2016–2017, was nominated to the Supreme Court in 2018 by the reconstituted National Council of the Judiciary, the body that selects judges, whose overhaul by the Law and Justice government was contested. He was appointed in February 2019 with no prior judicial experience. On 15 May 2020, after Kamil Zaradkiewicz resigned, President Andrzej Duda entrusted him with the duties of acting First President of the Supreme Court.
cite: Presidential decision of 15 May 2020; Ruleoflaw.pl

n: Black Hand leader Apis ran Serbia's military intelligence
rank: chief of intelligence, Serbian General Staff
d: Unification or Death, known as the Black Hand, was a secret society of Serbian army officers founded in 1911. In 1913 its leader, Dragutin Dimitrijević 'Apis', was appointed chief of General Staff intelligence of the Serbian army. Many scholars hold that he sanctioned the 1914 Sarajevo assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand, heir to the Austro-Hungarian throne, with the Black Hand supplying weapons and training; the killing led to the First World War. In 1917 Prince Regent Alexander had him court-martialled at Salonika for treason; he and two others were shot on 26 June 1917 and more than 200 members were imprisoned. In 1953 the Supreme Court of Serbia retried the case and acquitted them for lack of proof of the alleged plot against the Prince Regent.
cite: Salonika court-martial, 1917; Supreme Court of Serbia retrial, 1953; Encyclopaedia Britannica

n: White Hand officers' society saw its leader made Prime Minister
org_note: White Hand (Bela ruka): secret Serbian officers' group founded in 1912 by Petar Živković in opposition to the Black Hand.
rank: Prime Minister of the Kingdom of Yugoslavia
d: The White Hand (Bela ruka), a secret society of Serbian army officers, gained influence over the king and saw its leader appointed Prime Minister. It was founded in 1912 at the Hotel Paris in Belgrade by officers led by Petar Živković, as a rival to the Black Hand; Crown Prince Alexander later joined. After the Black Hand was broken at the 1917 Salonika trial, the White Hand gained influence over Alexander. When King Alexander I suspended the constitution on 6 January 1929 with White Hand officers' support and ruled as a dictator, General Živković was appointed Prime Minister, serving until 1932.
cite: Srejović, Gavrilović & Ćirković (eds.), Istorija srpskog naroda (1983); Milivoje Alimpić, Solunski front (1967)

n: Secret Masonic lodge's leader became Russia's Prime Minister
org_note: Lodge: Grand Orient of Russia's Peoples, an irregular Masonic body formed from Grand Orient de France lodges and openly separate from 1912.
rank: Minister of Justice, Minister of War, then Prime Minister
d: The Grand Orient of Russia's Peoples, a secret Masonic organisation, had its own leader at the head of Russia's government in 1917. Alexander Kerensky was its Secretary General from 1916 to mid-1917, succeeding Nikolai Nekrasov, who held the post in 1912–13 and 1914–16. After the February Revolution ended Tsarist rule, Kerensky served in the Provisional Government as Minister of Justice (March 1917), Minister for War (May) and Prime Minister (July). Historians describe most of the lodge's members as associated with the Provisional Government. The Bolsheviks overthrew that government in October 1917.
cite: Academic histories of the Russian Revolution (Alpha History summary; Grand Orient of Russia's Peoples records as published by historians)

n: P2 member Calvi convicted but kept control of Banco Ambrosiano
d: Roberto Calvi, chairman of Banco Ambrosiano and a member of the secret P2 Masonic lodge, stayed in charge of the bank even after a criminal conviction. In 1981, months after his name appeared on the P2 membership list seized by police, Calvi was sentenced to four years (suspended) and fined US$19.8 million for moving US$27 million out of Italy illegally, in breach of Italy's currency-export rules. He was released pending appeal and kept his post as chairman of Banco Ambrosiano. The following year the bank collapsed with about US$1.3 billion unaccounted for, and P2 head Licio Gelli was later convicted of fraud over it.
cite: Milan court, 1981 currency-export verdict

arch.t: Vatican-Masonic Network — Roberto Calvi Murder; Banco Ambrosiano Collapse; P2 Lodge Member Directed Vatican Bank Investments (PROVEN)

n: Banco Ambrosiano collapse: P2 head Gelli convicted of fraud
rank: private bank used by P2 members
d: The secret P2 Masonic lodge had a member, Roberto Calvi, at the head of Banco Ambrosiano, and its leader Licio Gelli was later convicted over the bank's fraudulent collapse. In 1982 Banco Ambrosiano could not account for about US$1.287 billion, much of it routed through offshore companies tied to the Vatican Bank (IOR), its main shareholder. The Bank of Italy had warned of problems in a 1978 report. The bank was replaced by Nuovo Banco Ambrosiano in August 1982. In April 1992 a Milan court convicted 33 people of fraud; P2 head Licio Gelli's sentence was set at 12 years, confirmed by the Court of Cassation in April 1998.
cite: Milan Tribunal, fraudulent-bankruptcy verdict April 1992; Court of Cassation April 1998

arch.t: Vatican-Masonic Network — Roberto Calvi Murder; Banco Ambrosiano Collapse; P2 Lodge Member Directed Vatican Bank Investments (PROVEN)

n: P2 membership list found: 962 names across Italy's state
d: Propaganda Due (P2), a Masonic lodge run in secret by businessman Licio Gelli, had placed members throughout Italy's parliament, government, armed forces and intelligence services, as a list found in 1981 showed. On 17 March 1981 Guardia di Finanza (financial police) officers under Col. Vincenzo Bianchi, sent by Milan magistrates Gherardo Colombo and Giuliano Turone who were investigating banker Michele Sindona, searched Gelli's Giole factory at Castiglion Fibocchi (Arezzo). They found a list of 962 names. It included 44 members of parliament, ministers, 195 military officers (12 Carabinieri generals, 5 Guardia di Finanza generals, 22 army generals, 4 air force generals, 8 admirals), and the heads of all three intelligence services. The government published it on 21 May 1981.
cite: Milan investigating magistrates' search of 17 March 1981; Italian government publication 21 May 1981

arch.t: Italian Parliamentary Commission CONFIRMED — P2 Lodge Infiltrated Government, Military, Intelligence, Media, and Banking as Parallel State (962 Documented Members)

n: P2 list brings down Prime Minister Forlani's government
d: The secret P2 Masonic lodge had members close to Italy's Prime Minister, and the discovery of its membership list in 1981 ended his government. Prime Minister Arnaldo Forlani's chef de cabinet (chief of staff) was on the list, and Forlani was accused of delaying its publication. Justice Minister Adolfo Sarti, listed as a candidate for membership, resigned first; Forlani handed his resignation to President Sandro Pertini three days later, in May 1981, bringing down his government. The list also named ministers, members of parliament, military officers and the heads of the intelligence services.
cite: Resignation of the Forlani government, May 1981; Time, 8 June 1981

arch.t: Italian Parliamentary Commission CONFIRMED — P2 Lodge Infiltrated Government, Military, Intelligence, Media, and Banking as Parallel State (962 Documented Members)

n: Two serving ministers and five undersecretaries on the P2 list
d: The secret P2 Masonic lodge counted members inside the sitting Italian cabinet. When its membership list was seized in 1981, two ministers in office in Arnaldo Forlani's cabinet appeared on it as full members: Foreign Trade Minister Enrico Manca (Socialist) and Labour Minister Franco Foschi (Christian Democrat). Five undersecretaries, the junior ministers below them, were also listed: Costantino Belluscio, Pasquale Bandiera, Francesco Fossa, Rolando Picchioni and Anselmo Martoni. Publication of the list led to the fall of Forlani's government in May 1981, and a parliamentary commission later described P2 as a criminal and subversive organisation.
cite: P2 membership list published 21 May 1981; Anselmi Commission

arch.t: Italian Parliamentary Commission CONFIRMED — P2 Lodge Infiltrated Government, Military, Intelligence, Media, and Banking as Parallel State (962 Documented Members)

n: Socialist MP Fabrizio Cicchitto admits P2 membership
rank: member of parliament, Socialist Party leadership
d: The secret P2 Masonic lodge had members in Italy's parliament: the membership list seized in 1981 named 44 parliamentarians and a party secretary. Fabrizio Cicchitto, a director of the Italian Socialist Party, was the only one of about 30 parliamentarians named in early press reports who admitted being a member. A parliamentary commission chaired by Tina Anselmi later described P2 as a criminal and subversive organisation, and a 1982 law dissolved it and banned secret associations that seek to interfere with public bodies.
cite: Time, 8 June 1981; P2 list

arch.t: Italian Parliamentary Commission CONFIRMED — P2 Lodge Infiltrated Government, Military, Intelligence, Media, and Banking as Parallel State (962 Documented Members)

n: Italy's Chief of Defence Staff, Adm. Torrisi, on the P2 list
rank: Chief of the Defence General Staff
d: The secret P2 Masonic lodge had Italy's most senior military officer among its members. Admiral Giovanni Torrisi, Chief of the Defence Staff, the head of all the armed forces, from 1 February 1980 to 29 September 1981, and before that navy chief of staff, appeared on the P2 membership list with card no. 631. The list was found by police in March 1981 and published in May. Torrisi left the post months after the list was published. A parliamentary commission later described P2, run by businessman Licio Gelli, as an organisation aiming to undermine Italian democracy.
cite: P2 membership list 1981; Anselmi Commission

arch.t: Italian Parliamentary Commission CONFIRMED — P2 Lodge Infiltrated Government, Military, Intelligence, Media, and Banking as Parallel State (962 Documented Members)

n: Military intelligence (SISMI) director Santovito on the P2 list
d: The secret P2 Masonic lodge had the head of Italy's military intelligence service among its members. General Giuseppe Santovito led SISMI, the military intelligence service, from its creation in 1978 until August 1981 and was on the P2 membership list found in 1981. Prime Minister Giovanni Spadolini removed him during the scandal, and the Anselmi Commission, parliament's inquiry into P2, questioned him. He was arrested in December 1983 on charges of disclosing secrets and died in February 1984 before trial. The heads of Italy's other two intelligence bodies were also on the list.
cite: P2 list 1981; Anselmi Commission hearings

arch.t: Italian Parliamentary Commission CONFIRMED — P2 Lodge Infiltrated Government, Military, Intelligence, Media, and Banking as Parallel State (962 Documented Members)

n: Domestic intelligence (SISDE) director Grassini enrolled in P2
d: The secret P2 Masonic lodge had the first head of Italy's domestic intelligence service among its members. General Giulio Grassini, appointed first director of SISDE, the civilian security service, in January 1978, was enrolled in P2 with card no. 515. He resigned when the membership list was found in 1981 and was replaced on 13 July 1981. In October 1981 the parliamentary commission on P2 heard him on possible intelligence involvement in the 1978 kidnapping of Aldo Moro, the former Prime Minister abducted and killed by the Red Brigades. The heads of Italy's other two intelligence bodies were also on the P2 list.
cite: P2 list 1981; Anselmi Commission hearing, October 1981

arch.t: Italian Parliamentary Commission CONFIRMED — P2 Lodge Infiltrated Government, Military, Intelligence, Media, and Banking as Parallel State (962 Documented Members)

n: Intelligence coordinator Walter Pelosi on the P2 list
d: The secret P2 Masonic lodge had members at the head of all three of Italy's intelligence bodies in 1981. Walter Pelosi led CESIS, the body that coordinated the military service SISMI and the civilian service SISDE on behalf of the Prime Minister, and he was on the P2 membership list seized that year, alongside SISMI director Giuseppe Santovito and SISDE director Giulio Grassini. A private lodge run by businessman Licio Gelli therefore had members in charge of the whole intelligence system. A parliamentary commission later described P2 as a criminal and subversive organisation.
cite: P2 membership list 1981; Anselmi Commission

arch.t: Italian Parliamentary Commission CONFIRMED — P2 Lodge Infiltrated Government, Military, Intelligence, Media, and Banking as Parallel State (962 Documented Members)

n: Former military intelligence (SID) chief Vito Miceli on P2 list
d: The secret P2 Masonic lodge counted a former head of Italy's military intelligence among its members. General Vito Miceli led army counter-intelligence (SIOS) in 1969–70 and the SID, Italy's main intelligence service at the time, from 1970 to 1974, and appears on the P2 list (file 491). Padua judges arrested him on 31 October 1974 in the 'Rosa dei Venti' inquiry into a secret military structure suspected of planning a coup; he was acquitted in 1978, and the acquittal was upheld in 1984 and 1985. He sat in parliament as a deputy for the neo-fascist MSI party from 1976 to 1987.
cite: Padua investigation 1974; acquittal 1978, Cassation 1985; P2 list

arch.t: Italian Parliamentary Commission CONFIRMED — P2 Lodge Infiltrated Government, Military, Intelligence, Media, and Banking as Parallel State (962 Documented Members)

n: Counter-intelligence chief Gianadelio Maletti on the P2 list
d: The secret P2 Masonic lodge listed the head of Italian military counter-intelligence among its members. General Gianadelio Maletti headed counter-intelligence at the SID, Italy's main intelligence service, from 1971 to 1975 and appears on the P2 list (file 499), though he denied joining. On 23 February 1979 the Catanzaro Court of Assizes sentenced him to 4 years for shielding Guido Giannettini and Marco Pozzan in the case of the 1969 Piazza Fontana bombing in Milan; the sentence was cut to 2 years and made final in 1987. He moved to South Africa in 1980.
cite: Catanzaro Court of Assizes, 23 Feb 1979; Bari Appeal Court of Assizes 1987

arch.t: Italian Parliamentary Commission CONFIRMED — P2 Lodge Infiltrated Government, Military, Intelligence, Media, and Banking as Parallel State (962 Documented Members)

n: Financial police commander Giannini on the P2 list
rank: commander-general of the Guardia di Finanza (financial police)
d: The secret P2 Masonic lodge had the commander of the Guardia di Finanza, Italy's financial police, among its members, the same force sent to search its leader's premises. Orazio Giannini appears on the P2 list with card no. 832. During the 17 March 1981 search of Licio Gelli's factory, the officer leading it, Col. Vincenzo Bianchi, received a call from the force's commander-general saying 'I am in those lists too.' The search found the membership list, which the government published in May 1981.
cite: P2 membership list 1981; Anselmi Commission

arch.t: Italian Parliamentary Commission CONFIRMED — P2 Lodge Infiltrated Government, Military, Intelligence, Media, and Banking as Parallel State (962 Documented Members)

n: Ex-financial police chief Giudice, P2 member, convicted of fuel fraud
rank: commander-general of the Guardia di Finanza 1974–1978
d: The secret P2 Masonic lodge counted a former commander of Italy's financial police among its members, and he was later convicted in a large tax-evasion case. General Raffaele Giudice commanded the Guardia di Finanza, which polices tax and customs, from 31 July 1974 to 20 November 1978 and appeared on the 1981 P2 list. In the 'oil scandal' (scandalo dei petroli), a scheme to evade taxes on fuel, the Turin Tribunal sentenced him on 30 April 1987 to 3 years 10 months at first instance; his case was separated on appeal.
cite: Turin Tribunal, 30 April 1987 (first instance)

arch.t: Italian Parliamentary Commission CONFIRMED — P2 Lodge Infiltrated Government, Military, Intelligence, Media, and Banking as Parallel State (962 Documented Members)

n: 195 military officers on the P2 list
rank: generals and admirals of all services
d: The secret P2 Masonic lodge had placed members across the top of Italy's armed forces. The membership list seized in 1981 included 195 officers: 12 Carabinieri generals (the military police), 5 Guardia di Finanza generals (the financial police), 22 army generals, 4 air force generals and 8 admirals. Names included Admiral Gino Birindelli and generals Giovanni Allavena, a former head of the SIFAR intelligence service, and Giovanbattista Palumbo of the Carabinieri. A parliamentary commission later described P2 as a criminal and subversive organisation aiming to undermine Italian democracy.
cite: P2 membership list 1981; Anselmi Commission final report 1984

arch.t: Italian Parliamentary Commission CONFIRMED — P2 Lodge Infiltrated Government, Military, Intelligence, Media, and Banking as Parallel State (962 Documented Members)

n: Anselmi Commission finds P2 aimed to undermine democracy
d: Propaganda Due (P2), a secret Masonic lodge run by businessman Licio Gelli, had placed members in Italy's parliament, cabinet, armed forces and all three intelligence services, as its membership list showed when it was seized in 1981. Parliament then set up an inquiry under Law 527 of 23 September 1981, chaired by Christian Democrat Tina Anselmi. The commission ran until 1984 and produced six reports. The majority report described P2 as a criminal and subversive organisation aiming to 'undermine our democracy'. A minority report by Massimo Teodori argued P2 was part of the system rather than an outgrowth of it.
cite: Parliamentary Commission of Inquiry into the P2 Masonic Lodge (Anselmi Commission), final report 1984

arch.t: Italian Parliamentary Commission CONFIRMED — P2 Lodge Infiltrated Government, Military, Intelligence, Media, and Banking as Parallel State (962 Documented Members)

n: P2's reach into the state led to Italy's 1982 ban on secret lodges
d: P2 (Propaganda Due), a secret Masonic lodge, had enrolled members across Italy's government, armed forces and intelligence services, and police seized its membership list in 1981. Parliament responded by outlawing such groups. Law no. 17 of 25 January 1982, known as the 'Anselmi law', dissolved P2 and made illegal secret associations that seek to interfere with public bodies. The Grand Orient of Italy, the main Masonic body, had already withdrawn the lodge's charter in 1974, so P2 had no recognition from regular Freemasonry when the list was found. The same law was used in the 2010s prosecution of the 'P3' group.
cite: Italian Law no. 17 of 25 January 1982

arch.t: Italian Parliamentary Commission CONFIRMED — P2 Lodge Infiltrated Government, Military, Intelligence, Media, and Banking as Parallel State (962 Documented Members)

n: P2 conspiracy trial ends with Gelli acquitted
rank: prosecution for conspiracy against the state
d: Rome prosecutors tried to prove in court that P2, the secret Masonic lodge whose members held posts across Italy's state, was a political conspiracy against the state. They charged lodge head Licio Gelli and others with that offence. The Rome court acquitted all defendants on 16 April 1994, and the Rome Court of Appeal confirmed the acquittal on 27 March 1996. Gelli was convicted in other cases, including the Banco Ambrosiano fraud and the cover-up of the Bologna bombing investigation, and the 1982 Anselmi law had already dissolved the lodge.
cite: Rome Court of Assizes 16 April 1994; Rome Court of Appeal 27 March 1996

arch.t: Italian Parliamentary Commission CONFIRMED — P2 Lodge Infiltrated Government, Military, Intelligence, Media, and Banking as Parallel State (962 Documented Members)

n: P2 head and P2 intelligence general faked Bologna evidence
d: The head of the secret P2 Masonic lodge and a P2 member serving as a general in SISMI, Italy's military intelligence service, planted false evidence to steer the investigation into the 1980 Bologna railway station bombing. On 13 January 1981 a suitcase of explosives, weapons and false papers was placed on the Taranto–Milan train to send the inquiry toward a false foreign lead. In 1995 the Court of Cassation made final the convictions of Licio Gelli, SISMI general Pietro Musumeci (P2 list no. 487), SISMI colonel Giuseppe Belmonte and SISMI collaborator Francesco Pazienza for aggravated calumny, meaning falsely implicating others in a crime. Musumeci's final sentence was 8 years 5 months.
cite: Bologna Appeal Court 1994; Court of Cassation 1995

arch.t: Italian Parliamentary Commission CONFIRMED — P2 Lodge Infiltrated Government, Military, Intelligence, Media, and Banking as Parallel State (962 Documented Members)

n: Interior Ministry intelligence chief D'Amato named in Bologna bombing
rank: head of the Interior Ministry's Ufficio Affari Riservati
d: The secret P2 Masonic lodge is reported to have had a member at the head of the Italian Interior Ministry's intelligence office. Federico Umberto D'Amato headed the ministry's confidential affairs office (Ufficio Affari Riservati), a domestic intelligence unit, and is reported as a P2 member. After his death, Bologna prosecutors in 2020 and the courts in the trial of Paolo Bellini named him among the organisers of the 2 August 1980 Bologna station bombing, which killed 85 people, and of its media handling. The same investigation named P2 head Licio Gelli as a financier of the attack.
cite: Procura generale di Bologna 2020; Bellini verdicts 2022–2025

arch.t: Italian Parliamentary Commission CONFIRMED — P2 Lodge Infiltrated Government, Military, Intelligence, Media, and Banking as Parallel State (962 Documented Members)

n: Senator Mario Tedeschi named in Bologna bombing cover-up
d: Mario Tedeschi, a senator for the neo-fascist MSI party and a journalist described as a member of the secret P2 Masonic lodge, was named by Bologna prosecutors in 2020 as having helped Interior Ministry intelligence chief Federico Umberto D'Amato manage press coverage of the 1980 Bologna station bombing, which killed 85 people, and mislead the inquiry. The same investigation named P2 head Licio Gelli as a financier of the attack. Tedeschi was dead and could not be charged.
cite: Procura generale di Bologna, 2020

arch.t: Italian Parliamentary Commission CONFIRMED — P2 Lodge Infiltrated Government, Military, Intelligence, Media, and Banking as Parallel State (962 Documented Members)

n: P2 head Licio Gelli: Argentine post, prison escape, conviction
d: Licio Gelli, head of the secret P2 Masonic lodge, had ties inside Argentina's state as well as Italy's: he held an Argentine honorary diplomatic post and is linked to Argentine P2 members Emilio Massera, a navy commander in the military junta, and José López Rega, a government minister. After the lodge was exposed, Gelli was arrested in Geneva in September 1982, escaped Champ-Dollon prison on 10 August 1983 and was extradited to Italy in February 1988. His 12-year sentence for the Banco Ambrosiano fraud was confirmed in April 1998; he vanished in May 1998 and was arrested in Cannes that September.
cite: Court of Cassation, April 1998

arch.t: Vatican-Masonic Network — Roberto Calvi Murder; Banco Ambrosiano Collapse; P2 Lodge Member Directed Vatican Bank Investments (PROVEN)

n: Andreotti reveals Gladio, a NATO-coordinated secret network
d: Gladio, the Italian branch of the secret 'stay-behind' networks that NATO countries set up to resist a possible Soviet invasion, operated within Italy's intelligence services under NATO coordination and without public knowledge. On 24 October 1990 Prime Minister Giulio Andreotti told the Chamber of Deputies that a secret stay-behind 'structure of information, response and safeguard' had existed since the 1950s under NATO coordination. He gave the parliamentary massacres commission a list of 622 civilians, said 127 arms caches had been dismantled, and denied any role in bombings. On 22 November 1990 the European Parliament called on member states to dismantle such networks, and inquiries followed in Belgium, Switzerland and elsewhere.
cite: Statement to the Chamber of Deputies 24 Oct 1990; European Parliament resolution 22 Nov 1990

arch.t: Italy — Operation Gladio: NATO Stay-Behind Network Used for Domestic Terrorism; 'Strategy of Tension'

n: NATO-linked secret Gladio network inside Italy's intelligence had 622 members
d: A secret armed 'stay-behind' network called Gladio was run inside SISMI, Italy's military intelligence service, under NATO coordination, and was kept from parliament until Prime Minister Giulio Andreotti disclosed it in October 1990. A stay-behind network is a group of trained people meant to resist an occupying army. Parliament's commission on terrorism and massacres then questioned SISMI. On 29 November 1990 General Paolo Inzerilli, SISMI chief of staff, told it that 'the true number is 622': 215 active, 339 reserve, 65 dead and 3 'frozen' members of the network's units.
cite: Parliamentary Commission on Terrorism and Massacres, hearing of 29 Nov 1990

arch.t: Italy — Operation Gladio: NATO Stay-Behind Network Used for Domestic Terrorism; 'Strategy of Tension'

n: P3 secret group convicted for seeking influence over the state
rank: network pressing on judges and state appointments
d: The 'P3', named after the earlier P2 lodge, was a secret group that prosecutors said sought undue influence on the Italian state. On 16 March 2018 a Rome court convicted eight people in the case. Businessman Flavio Carboni received 6 years 6 months for secret association; Arcangelo Martino 4 years 9 months under the Anselmi law, the 1982 law against secret societies that seek to interfere with public bodies. Senator Denis Verdini was acquitted of secret association but given 1 year 3 months for illegal party funding. In the same verdict a senior judge, Vincenzo Carbone, was convicted of abuse of office.
cite: Rome Tribunal, P3 verdict 16 March 2018
org_note: P3: secret association prosecuted under the 1982 Anselmi law, named by press after P2

n: Senior judge Vincenzo Carbone convicted in the P3 case
rank: senior judge (former First President of the Court of Cassation)
d: The 'P3', a secret group that prosecutors said sought undue influence on the Italian state, reached a senior judge. In the 16 March 2018 Rome verdict that convicted the group's organisers of secret association, Vincenzo Carbone received a 2-year suspended sentence for abuse of office, meaning use of a public post for improper ends. Former undersecretary Nicola Cosentino received a 10-month suspended term for defamation and private violence. Charges against Sardinia regional president Ugo Cappellacci lapsed.
cite: Rome Tribunal, P3 verdict 16 March 2018
org_note: P3: secret association prosecuted under the 1982 Anselmi law

n: P4 network: MP Alfonso Papa passed secrets to fixer Bisignani
d: Luigi Bisignani, a go-between, was accused of running a hidden network, called the 'P4', that reached into Italy's parliament and justice system to gather confidential information and favours. In the 2011 'P4' inquiry, Alfonso Papa, a deputy for Silvio Berlusconi's PdL party, a former Naples prosecutor and Justice Ministry director, was accused of passing confidential information to Bisignani and pressing businessmen for favours. The Chamber authorised his arrest in July 2011 and he spent 101 days in Poggioreale prison. Bisignani took a plea of 1 year 7 months. Papa was convicted in 2016 (4 years 6 months), but the charges lapsed on appeal by 2021; the judiciary's disciplinary body removed him from the bench in 2023.
cite: Naples courts 2016–2021; Superior Council of the Judiciary (CSM) disciplinary section 2023
org_note: P4: press name for the Bisignani information-trading network

n: Mafia use of lodges: Anti-Mafia Commission seizes lodge lists
d: Mafia groups in Sicily and Calabria were suspected of using Masonic lodges to reach officials and businesses, and Italy's parliamentary Anti-Mafia Commission forced the lodges to reveal who belonged. On 1 March 2017 the Commission, chaired by Rosy Bindi, voted unanimously to seize membership lists of lodges in Sicily and Calabria from 1990 onward, after grand masters missed an 8 February deadline citing privacy. The Guardia di Finanza, Italy's financial police, searched the headquarters of the Grand Orient of Italy, the Regular Grand Lodge of Italy, the Serenissima Gran Loggia and the Gran Loggia d'Italia. In 2024 the European Court of Human Rights found the seizure breached Article 8 (the right to privacy); its Grand Chamber upheld that in July 2026.
cite: Parliamentary Anti-Mafia Commission decision of 1 March 2017; ECHR, Grande Oriente d'Italia v. Italy

n: Anti-Mafia report finds 193 lodge members in mafia cases
d: Italy's parliamentary Anti-Mafia Commission found people involved in mafia cases sitting in Masonic lodges in Sicily and Calabria, and proposed keeping judges, soldiers and police out of lodges. Its report on mafia and Freemasonry, presented by chair Rosy Bindi in December 2017 after the lodges' membership lists were seized, found that 193 people listed in lodges were recorded in organised-crime proceedings by the National Anti-Mafia Directorate, the national prosecutors' office for mafia cases. It recommended extending bans on lodge membership to magistrates, career military and police.
cite: Parliamentary Anti-Mafia Commission, report on mafia and Freemasonry, December 2017

arch.t: UK Investigation: Masonic Network in Police and Judiciary Led to Parliamentary Inquiry and New Legal Disclosure Requirements

n: Castelvetrano: most of town executive were Freemasons
rank: town executive and council (home town of Matteo Messina Denaro)
d: Italy's Anti-Mafia Commission, investigating whether mafia groups used Masonic lodges to reach public bodies, found heavy Masonic membership in a Sicilian town government, a local bank and a Calabrian health authority. Its 2017 report found that in Castelvetrano, in Trapani province, in 2016, 4 of the 5 town assessors (members of the mayor's executive) and 7 of 30 councillors were Freemasons. It also found that 11 executives and staff of a Trapani-area cooperative bank belonged to a Grand Orient lodge, and a significant Masonic presence in senior posts at the Locri health authority in Calabria.
cite: Parliamentary Anti-Mafia Commission, report on mafia and Freemasonry, December 2017

n: 'Ndrangheta trial convicts officials and ex-senator Pittelli
rank: former senator and Forza Italia regional coordinator
d: The Mancuso clan of the 'Ndrangheta, the Calabrian mafia, drew in civil servants, police and politicians, and prosecutors say a former senator linked it to Masonic circles and business. In the Rinascita Scott maxi-trial against the clan, more than 200 of over 300 defendants were convicted in November 2023, including civil servants, a former police chief and a former mayor. Lawyer and former Forza Italia senator Giancarlo Pittelli, described by prosecutors as a Freemason linking the clan to Masonic circles and business, received 11 years for collusion. In a separate 'Mala Pigna' trial the Palmi Tribunal gave him 14 years in 2025 for external complicity, meaning helping a mafia group without being a member.
cite: Vibo Valentia Tribunal, Rinascita Scott verdict November 2023; Palmi Tribunal 2025

n: Communion and Liberation figure Formigoni led Lombardy for 18 years
d: Comunione e Liberazione (Communion and Liberation, CL), an Italian Catholic lay movement, had its unofficial political spokesman at the head of Lombardy, Italy's richest region. Roberto Formigoni led Lombardy from 1995 to 2013. On 21 February 2019 the Court of Cassation confirmed his corruption conviction in the Maugeri health-care case, with a final sentence of 5 years 10 months. The court ruling concerned bribes, not the movement itself.
cite: Italian Court of Cassation, 21 February 2019

n: Opus Dei members enter Franco's cabinet and redirect the economy
d: Opus Dei, a Catholic organisation of lay people and priests, had members placed at the head of Spain's economic ministries under the dictator Francisco Franco. In February 1957 Franco appointed two Opus Dei members: Mariano Navarro Rubio as finance minister and Alberto Ullastres as trade minister. Both served until 1965 and drove the Stabilisation Plan that ended autarky, the policy of economic self-sufficiency, and opened Spain to foreign trade and investment. Historians count 8 Opus Dei members among Franco's 116 ministers, none before 1957. By 1969 eleven members of the cabinet had ties to the organisation.
cite: Academic history (Preston; Crozier; Messori; John Allen)

n: Opus Dei member Navarro Rubio: finance minister, then central bank
rank: Finance Minister 1957–65; Governor of the Bank of Spain 1965–70
d: Opus Dei, a Catholic organisation of lay people and priests, had one of its members run Spain's finances and then its central bank.
